newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money steady at 13.0/14.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money steady at 13.0/14.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 13.0/14.0 percent on Monday morning on sufficient liquidity.
Dealers said liquidity was ample despite a neutral central bank money policy, but operators were worried about a possible tightening on Tuesday due to weekly tax payments.
One local bank dealer said operators seemed to anticipate some tightening on Tuesday because tax payments in the second week were usually higher, and longer-term rates were firm.
One-week money was at 12.75/13.00 percent and one-month at 13.25/13.375 percent.
The central bank kept its bilateral rates stable, offering one-week bilateral papers (SBIs) at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.5 percent, one- and three-month at 10.25 and 11.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 10.13 percent, compared with 13.87 percent on Wednesday.

Bond dealers said trading was slow, with focus seen on upcoming primary issues, including the 500 billion rupiah seven-year straight bonds of Bank DKI, the 250 billion rupiah of PT Bunas Finance, the 150 billion rupiah issue from Bank NISP and the 300 billion rupiah bonds of PT Suryamas Dutamakmur.
They said brisk interest was seen in the Bank DKI bonds.
One dealer said prices of PLN V B/96 bonds softened by 25 basis points. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
